summary: A cast-iron tower marking Pass Cavallo, first lit in 1852, wrecked by war and the sea, rebuilt inland and relit in 1873, relit again in 1999.

notes_for_editor: Primary Light-House Board reports for 1852-1886 are not in the corpus, so the construction, Civil War, 1865 and 1886 episodes rest on LighthouseFriends, the Calhoun County Historical Commission narrative and the Calhoun County Museum timeline, which disagree on: first lighting day (31 Dec vs 'December'; Wikipedia says 21 Dec, uncited), daymark date, 1857/58/59 raising and lens, 4th vs 5th order temporary lens, 1862 destruction attempt, distance of the move (2 miles vs the 1873 notice's OCR-damaged figure, perhaps 1.5), 1870 vs 1872-73 move, Barr's succession (1946 roster vs 1948 LF), foundation formation (1997 vs 1998), ownership (TPWD vs USFWS lease to Calhoun County), $905,000 grant vs $1.23M renovation. NRHP nomination text not digitized. Whether the modern solar light is currently lit was not confirmed (record says conflicting). Bulletin OCR is noisy; quotes in the text of Olsen's letter are OCR-cleaned and the keeper's name matched from OCR 'Ol sen'. Roster lines come from USLHS; Cecil C. Houston is from LighthouseFriends only; spelling variants Herman/Hermann Schrieber, Forrestier/Forestier, Stephen D./P. Hill. 1929 Bulletin storm date given as June 28 (year taken from the bulletin volume and the adjacent item dated 1929). Commissioner 1922 work list for Matagorda (wharf, walks, fence under an appropriation of 6 March 1920) was found but not used. Bulletin item names for 1921 tug and 1922 launch not used (OCR).
